nodes.label: Migration decision tree (five tools)
nodes.rationale: The five migration tools look superficially similar, so the guide is a decision tree: new field with a default goes to defaultsAdapter, rename/restructure to migratingAdapter, multi-service shared schema to the SchemaRegistry, on-write validation to validatedEventAdapter, pre-envelope journal to wrapEventAsEnvelope. Most changes pick exactly one; they compose, but not all combinations make sense.

nodes.label: validatedEventAdapter
nodes.rationale: Wraps any existing adapter in a codec so every write is validated before it lands in the journal — catching a wrong type that sneaked through JSON.parse at the persist call rather than at recovery three days later. Reads trust the journal because it was validated at write.

nodes.label: InMemorySchemaRegistry (recipe 3)
nodes.rationale: For schemas not owned by one actor — several services writing one Kafka topic or shared journal, each possibly on a different version. Registration is a first-class step, so a service version can refuse to start when its schema breaks the configured compatibility level. Not worth it for single-service single-actor evolution.

nodes.label: migrateBetweenJournals
nodes.rationale: Copies and optionally transforms a journal between two backends. It reproduces compaction: the target's compaction mark is raised to just below the first surviving event before appending, so every event lands on the sequence number it had in the source.

nodes.label: A sequence number is a reference, not an ordinal
nodes.rationale: The paired snapshot, every read-side offset and every projection cursor names (persistenceId, sequenceNr). Renumbering a compacted tail detaches all of them at once, and in the layout compaction normally leaves behind — the snapshot sitting at the compaction point — nothing fails loudly: recovery folds a later tail onto an earlier state and the actor serves commands from a state that never existed. Hence copy the journal before the snapshots, and a target that cannot implement raiseCompactionMark throws CompactedSourceError instead of renumbering.

nodes.label: Never rename a manifest
nodes.rationale: The manifest string is the identity of the event type across the lifetime of the journal, so renaming it breaks every historical entry. If it must change, write a new manifest at version 1 and use migrateBetweenJournals with an eventTransform into a fresh target.

nodes.label: Source and target persistence options are separate
nodes.rationale: A re-key sweep is an ordinary reason to migrate, so source and target routinely hold different keys or keyrings — hence sourcePersistenceOptions and targetPersistenceOptions are passed separately. Omitting targetPersistenceOptions on a target that encrypts per call silently resolves to { mode: 'none' } and the migrated snapshot lands in the bucket as plaintext.
